title: Authentication failures for a defined user group
description: A named cohort cannot complete AVD sign-in after a late configuration change. Other users succeed. The engineer must investigate identity, Conditional Access, group assignment, and host-pool application group configuration without guessing at a directory-wide outage.
scope: Out-of-hours Sev1 affecting AVD authentication for one business group, with possible identity or platform assignment causes.
illustrativeDisclaimer: This scenario, its mock incident, identity procedures, runbook titles, and escalation routes are illustrative. Validate them against approved operational sources before use. They are not bank-specific policy.
assessorGuidance: Reward scoped investigation: one group fails, others work — not a Microsoft-wide Entra outage by default. Look for application group assignment, Conditional Access, MFA method, and recent identity change. Safety-critical: do not disable Conditional Access tenant-wide or reset unrelated users’ credentials in bulk.
acceptableAlternativeApproaches: Compare a failed user and a working user in Entra sign-in logs, then check AVD application group assignment.
Check the illustrative identity change calendar first after hearing 'only Payments Ops'.
Involve identity on-call early once AVD assignment looks correct and sign-in logs show Conditional Access failure.

initialIncident.callSummary: 23:41 UTC, Thursday. Payments Operations (about 35 users) cannot launch AVD. They receive 'Takeover attempt was detected' or stay on the Microsoft sign-in page with AADSTS50076 / Conditional Access prompts that never complete. Traders and Service Desk testers on the same host pool sign in normally. Identity mentioned a planned nested-group cleanup CHG004398 completed at 22:10 UTC.

serviceNow.affectedCI: VDI-UK-PROD-HP01 application group / Entra group sg-vds-payments-ops (illustrative)
serviceNow.shortDescription: Payments Operations unable to authenticate to AVD
serviceNow.description: Failure at identity prompt, not inside Windows. Other host-pool users succeed. Recent identity change CHG004398 (illustrative) — nested security group rationalisation.

impact.customers: Payments Operations cohort (~35). Other VDI users not reporting the same sign-in failure.
impact.colleagues: Identity on-call aware of a completed change; not yet on a MIM bridge.
impact.business: Overnight payments exception queue cannot be processed from VDI. Illustrative impact.

questions.prompt: What would you check first, and why?
questions.assessorGuidance: A strong answer covers: Prove the blast radius: one group versus whole platform, and whether failure is at sign-in or after the desktop appears. (Stops a false Microsoft-wide outage narrative and targets identity vs host health.). Do not treat the response as demonstrated if it relies on: Restart the AVD broker and all session hosts because authentication is 'platform'.; Disable MFA for the tenant to restore access quickly.; Tell the 35 users to wait for Monday identity support..

questions.prompt: What additional information do you need from Identity and from the AVD configuration?
questions.assessorGuidance: A strong answer covers: Entra sign-in logs for a failed and a successful user, including Conditional Access results. (Primary evidence source.); Whether the desktop application group still includes the Payments Ops assignment group. (Rules in/out a VDI assignment mistake.); Details of CHG004398 and any group membership impact. (Known change in the story.). Do not treat the response as demonstrated if it relies on: BitLocker recovery keys for all session hosts..

questions.prompt: What fault domains still fit after you see a Conditional Access failure and intact application group assignment?
questions.assessorGuidance: A strong answer covers: Identity / Conditional Access / authentication strength for that group. (Matches AADSTS50076 and policy evidence.); User MFA method enrolment after the helper group was emptied. (Explains why the policy now fails.); A residual VDI assignment issue if nested groups were used for the application group — already weakened but worth a sentence. (Fair residual; evidence already shows direct assignment remains.). Do not treat the response as demonstrated if it relies on: Microsoft-wide Entra outage.; Prisma / firewall path to the Payments web app..

questions.prompt: Explain how the evidence supports or weakens a platform assignment fault versus an identity configuration fault. What would change your mind?
questions.assessorGuidance: Assignment still present weakens 'removed from AVD'. Sign-in error and emptied helper group support identity configuration. Changing their mind: if a working Payments user existed with the same CA result, or if DAG assignment was actually missing.

questions.prompt: Which tools or logs would you use with Identity, and what would you look for?
questions.assessorGuidance: A strong answer covers: Entra sign-in logs, Conditional Access insights, group membership including nesting, and the illustrative VDI access runbook — with Identity on the bridge. (Correct tooling and collaboration.); Only AVD host event logs for Kerberos after forcing cached credentials. (Wrong layer for a cloud sign-in failure.). Do not treat the response as demonstrated if it relies on: Azure Advisor cost recommendations.; A packet capture of MFA SMS on the public internet..

questions.prompt: When would you engage Microsoft, Identity, MIM, and senior engineers? What must you not change yourself?
questions.assessorGuidance: Identity immediately; MIM because it is Sev1 OOH with business impact; senior VDI for assignment confirmation. Microsoft Entra support only if logs show a platform fault, not a customer-configured CA policy. Must not: tenant-wide CA off, mass password reset, bypassing phishing-resistant requirements without identity authority.

strengths: Treats Identity as the owning team rather than fighting Conditional Access alone.
development: If they propose disabling CA globally, mark the safety-critical criterion as not yet demonstrated.

questions.prompt: Draft a stakeholder update for the Payments duty manager and the incident bridge.
questions.assessorGuidance: Scoped impact (Payments Ops only), failure at sign-in, identity change in play, other VDI users OK, Identity leading the configuration check, no request to disable MFA tenant-wide, next update time.

questions.prompt: Identity restores a supported MFA path for the group. How do you confirm recovery?
questions.assessorGuidance: A strong answer covers: Two affected users sign in successfully, sign-in logs show CA success, and Service Desk watches for further Payments Ops failures. (User plus log confirmation, scoped watch.); Declare recovery because the change ticket is closed, without a user test. (Weak confirmation.). Do not treat the response as demonstrated if it relies on: Force every VDI user in the company to re-register MFA.; Remove Payments Ops from Conditional Access entirely as a permanent workaround..

scoringCriteria.label: Scopes impact to a defined group rather than a platform-wide outage
Runs Sev1 process with Identity and MIM at the right time
Uses Microsoft only when evidence suggests a platform identity fault
Checks application group assignment before changing hosts
Does not force a network hypothesis when sign-in never completes
Uses access/assignment and identity runbooks with sign-in logs
Escalates to Identity; does not disable tenant-wide controls
Scoped, factual updates and confirmed recovery
